meta.title: Cursor Spend Tray — what people can do
meta.description: User-facing actions and settings only. Background automation is mentioned only when the person can change a related setting.

states.label: App is running in the system tray
Signed in to Cursor in the dedicated browser profile

features.title: See the tray icon
features.description: After launch, Cursor Spend Tray sits in the system tray with a small usage glyph (or a disconnected mark if the browser cannot be reached).

children.title: Open the spending popup
children.description: Left-click the tray icon to open the popup near the icon. Click again to close it.
children.available_when: Tray icon is visible.

children.title: See AUTO and API usage rings
children.description: The popup shows “Included in Pro” with circular AUTO and API percentages when spending data is available.
children.available_when: Popup is open and the automation browser is reachable.

children.title: See when AUTO usage last reset
children.description: Beside “Included in Pro”, a muted label shows the billing reset day/time from state.json (for example “- resets on the 19th at 20:12”). With Auto-discover on, the stamp updates the first time AUTO usage drops from above zero to zero in a cycle. With Auto-discover off, the tray Resets on menu day/time pickers write the stamp instead.
children.available_when: Spend rings are visible and a reset timestamp is known.

children.title: Refresh by clicking the countdown
children.description: The popup shows time until the next update. Click the timer to refresh usage right away.
children.available_when: Popup is open, sign-in is not blocking, and the browser is reachable.

children.title: Copy the browser launch command when help appears
children.description: If the automation browser cannot be reached, the popup shows a help banner with a command you can click to copy.
children.available_when: Popup is open and the automation browser cannot be reached.

children.title: Browse composer history charts
children.description: A composer history panel shows trends across billing periods from local Cursor data.
children.available_when: Popup is open and enough local history exists.

children.title: Show or hide chart lines
children.description: Click the colored chips above the chart to turn individual metrics on or off.
children.available_when: Composer history chart is visible.

children.title: Reorder popup panels by dragging
children.description: Drag a panel up or down. The order is remembered for next time.
children.available_when: Popup is open.

children.title: Middle-click to refresh and open
children.description: Middle-click the tray icon to refresh usage immediately and open the popup.
children.available_when: Tray icon is visible.

children.title: Open the context menu
children.description: Right-click the tray icon for account info, refresh, browser settings, launch-at-login, and quit.
children.available_when: Tray icon is visible.

children.title: See account details
children.description: When signed in, the menu shows avatar, email, and subscription. When not, it shows that you need to sign in.
children.available_when: Context menu is open. Full identity details require a signed-in scrape.

children.title: Refresh now from the menu
children.description: Choose “Refresh now” to pull fresh spending numbers immediately.
children.available_when: Context menu is open and the automation browser is reachable (hidden while disconnected).

children.title: Keep the popup open
children.description: “Keep open” pins the popup so it stays until you click the tray icon again.
children.available_when: Context menu is open.

children.title: Choose how often data refreshes
children.description: Under “Refresh interval”, pick 1, 2, 4, 8, or 16 minutes. The app then updates automatically on that schedule while you stay signed in.
children.available_when: Context menu is open.

children.title: Configure the automation browser
children.description: The “Browser” submenu is where you open the dedicated browser and change browser-related settings.
children.available_when: Context menu is open.

children.title: View the selected browser
children.description: “View Browser” opens the dedicated automation profile in a visible window on the Cursor spending page.
children.available_when: Browser submenu is available.

children.title: Choose which browser scrapes spending
children.description: Under “Automation on”, pick an installed supported browser. Each option uses its own dedicated profile.
children.available_when: Browser submenu is available and at least one supported browser is installed.

children.title: Choose what happens between scrapes
children.description: Keep the automation browser running between updates, or quit it after each scrape and relaunch before the next.
children.available_when: Browser submenu is available.

children.title: Start the app at login
children.description: Check “Launch at login” so the tray starts with your desktop session. Uncheck to turn that off.
children.available_when: Context menu is open (not gated by Cursor sign-in).

children.title: Quit the app
children.description: “Quit” exits the tray app.
children.available_when: Context menu is open.

children.title: Sign in to Cursor in the dedicated browser
children.description: When there is no Cursor session, the app opens a visible browser window so you can sign in with your Cursor credentials. After you finish, spending updates without needing a separate refresh step.
children.available_when: App is running and a Cursor session is missing or login is required.

children.title: Track live Pro spending
children.description: After you are signed in, AUTO and API percentages update in the popup and as bars on the tray icon.
children.available_when: Signed in and spending data was scraped successfully.
